theReadThatPassed.shape: JSON:API. data[].type='budget'; data[].id string; data[].attributes = {name:string, entityId:string, coaId:string, budgetPeriods:array, workforceId:null|string, createdAt:string, updatedAt:string}
theReadThatPassed.isBastrops: Yes. Every one of the 12 records carries entityId 3c8981ac-1a8b-463d-b26b-5ef37c66734f, the Bastrop entity id hardcoded in server/services/opengov-bnp.ts. Budget names are Bastrop's own: FY2026 Operating Budget, FY2027 Operating Budget (WORKING), FY2026-2030 CIP Budget, FY2027-2031 CIP Budget.
theReadThatPassed.noPiiInShape: The endpoint returns no personal data. No field was redacted because none needed to be.

theReadThatPassed.whyThisIsTheOneThatMatters: This is the Finance lens's ADOPTED BUDGET required source, and it reproduces the operator capture's page-1 and page-2 figures exactly, at the digit, from the live source: capture adoptedBudget.expenses = total $69.6M / base $74.3M / adjustments -$4.3M, live = 69,579,851 / 74,349,204 / -4,769,353; capture revenue = total $74.6M / base $73.4M / +$1.1M, live = 74,568,390 / 73,425,092 / +1,143,298. The capture's 'Budget selected: FY2027 Operating Budget (WORKING)' also matches the live budget name.
theReadThatPassed.consequence: The design's 'Adopted budget -> MEASURED' is TRUE of the source and was never a screenshot artefact. What does not exist is the v1 platform route and the v2 adapter shape+grant. That gap is exactly G-159.

theReadThatFailed.endpoint: GET https://bastrop.opengov.com/api/v1/entities  and  GET https://bastrop.opengov.com/api/v1/reports  (what server/services/opengov.ts calls, and what a v1 platform route built on it would expose)
theReadThatFailed.result: Both return HTTP 200 and a 32-record catalog. ZERO of the 32 entities and ZERO of the 32 reports are Bastrop's.
theReadThatFailed.measured: entities.subdomain matched against 'bastrop' + name matched /bastrop/i -> 0 of 32. Reports matched against the code's own BASTROP_ENTITY_SLUGS = ['bastrop','bastroptx','bastrop-tx','cityofbastrop'] -> 0 of 32. First entity is '11th Judicial Circuit of Florida' (subdomain 11thjudicialcourtfl, state FL); first report is entity 'bonnercountyid'.
theReadThatFailed.whyItHappens: server/services/opengov.ts:119-121 filters reports by those four slugs and returns the filter's result, so getReports() returns an empty array for Bastrop. getEntities() has no Bastrop filter at all and returns the whole 32-row global catalog.
theReadThatFailed.consequence: A v1 platform route on this leg would put 32 non-Bastrop entities behind a Bastrop-named bridge, and getReports() would return []. Building it would be the 'silent fallback' defect class (DEV_PROCESS 4.3) with a Bastrop label on it.

credentialSurprise.finding: The key NAMED for BNP does not answer for Bastrop; the key NAMED for the v1 REST API does.
credentialSurprise.measured: Same /budgets request, two keys, same entityId: smartcity-OPENGOV_API_KEY -> 200, 3841 bytes, meta.totalRecords 12. smartcity-OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY -> 200, 161 bytes, body {"data":[],"links":{...},"meta":{"totalRecords":0}}. A Bearer-scheme control with the BNP key returned 401, confirming the scheme is Token and the key itself is the difference, not the header.
credentialSurprise.whyTheDeployedCodeStillWorks: server/services/opengov-bnp.ts:5-7 getBnpApiKey() returns process.env.OPENGOV_API_KEY || process.env.OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY - the v1-named variable is read FIRST. So in production, BNP calls are authenticated with the v1 key, which is the one that answers.
credentialSurprise.whyItMatters: This is a latent trap. OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY looks like the BNP credential and is not. Any future lane that 'tidies' getBnpApiKey() to prefer its own namesake would silently take BNP to zero budgets - and a lens reading that would render UNACCOUNTED for a city whose budget is in fact readable. Reported, NOT fixed: it is a credential-provisioning question for the operator, not a code fix this lane should make on a production service.

alsoMeasured.whyThisRetroExplainsTheCapture: The capture's 'Actual Spent is the Budget column copied' is what v1 falls back to when the actuals endpoints fail. The design's stance ('actuals are unaccounted') is therefore not a preference; it has a live basis: the source returns 500 for actuals today.
alsoMeasured.netPositionIsDerivable: The capture's netPosition $5.0M is revenues proposed 74,568,390 minus expenses proposed 69,579,851 = 4,988,539, i.e. $5.0M. Derivable, not separately published; the bridge should expose the parts and let the consumer derive, never ship a pre-derived net position as if measured.

scopeCorrection.whatTheDispatchAssumed: STEP 1: 'Map the Finance lens design's required sources ... to the v1 OpenGov, budgeting-and-planning and permit-revenue data. Add platform routes only for what the design uses.'
scopeCorrection.whatIsTrue: The design's four required sources map as: adopted budget -> BNP (budgets + amounts-summary + chart-of-accounts), and it ANSWERS. Permit fee revenue -> the DB-backed finance.ts mygov_fees routes, to be verified separately. Fund ledger -> absent everywhere. Department spend -> absent everywhere.
scopeCorrection.theDeliberateExclusion: No v1 platform route will be built on the v1-REST leg (opengov.ts: entities/reports/financial). It returns no Bastrop data, so it serves none of the design's four sources, and exposing 32 non-Bastrop entities under a platform route would be a false bridge. This is a named exclusion, not an omission (DEV_PROCESS 3.3).
